title: Cross-Linguistic Acoustic Biomarkers of Cognitive Impairment Across Interactive and Single-Speaker Speech Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2611.17710v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multilingual dementia detection is essential for scalable and equitable screening. In recent years, automated speech analysis has emerged as a promising approach for supporting dementia detection by enabling non-invasive and scalable assessment of cognitive function. However, existing studies that use automated speech analysis often rely on one type of task, such as picture description, and use black-box models. These studies often neglect the role of task and language. To address these gaps, we performed a cross-linguistic and cross-task acoustic analysis that integrates a conversational dataset with structured speech tasks across four languages (Spanish, Mandarin, English, Japanese). We applied statistical, linguist-/clinician-guided, and machine learning model-based feature selection to derive compact acoustic feature sets while maintaining classification performance. translated_title: 跨语言认知障碍声学生物标志物研究：交互式与单人语音任务对比
translated_abstract: 多语言痴呆症检测对于实现可扩展且公平的筛查至关重要。近年来，自动化语音分析已成为支持痴呆症检测的一种有前景的方法，它能够以非侵入式、可扩展的方式评估认知功能。然而，现有的自动化语音分析研究通常只依赖单一类型的任务（如图片描述），并使用黑盒模型，往往忽视了任务类型和语言本身的作用。为填补这些空白，我们开展了一项跨语言、跨任务的声学分析，将对话式数据集与涵盖四种语言（西班牙语、普通话、英语、日语）的结构化语音任务相结合。我们综合运用统计学方法、语言学家/临床医生指导的方法以及基于机器学习模型的特征选择方法，在保持分类性能的同时提取出紧凑的声学特征集，从而能够系统地比较与认知障碍相关的声学特征。
tldr: 该研究通过对西班牙语、普通话、英语和日语四种语言中对话式与结构化语音任务的跨语言、跨任务声学分析，结合统计、专家指导和机器学习三种特征选择方法，提取出紧凑可解释的声学生物标志物，为多语言认知障碍检测提供了可扩展且公平的筛查方案。
en_tdlr: This study performs a cross-linguistic, cross-task acoustic analysis across Spanish, Mandarin, English, and Japanese, integrating conversational and structured speech tasks with statistical, expert-guided, and machine learning feature selection to derive compact, interpretable acoustic biomarkers for scalable and equitable multilingual cognitive impairment screening.
